data.name: The Multidimensional Underwear Drawer
data.detailed_description:
The Multidimensional Underwear Drawer is an otome visual novel, in which young Hana finds eternal love … or death!

After a long time, Hana is single again. The breakup with her boyfriend Jan has hit her quite hard. While her best friend Kerstin and her childhood friend Furio try their best to free Hana from her depression, she focuses completely on her work and drowns herself in self-pity on the weekend.
But her gloomy mood summons two entities far worse: Two demons start inhabiting her apartment, in order to feed off her strained soul: Tymoteusz and Einar – One residing in her underwear drawer (which he also has happened to turn into a gate to hell itself), while the other possesses her teddy bear.
Adding to that chaos, her neighbor Blanche seems to have taken a rather special interest in Hana as well.
It’s the dawn of a hard time for her: Two demons occupying her home, a lesbian besieging her and two friends constantly pampering her. On top of all that, her ex shows up to reconquer his lost love …

Which way will be the right one for Hana? Which will lead to bliss? Which will lead to loneliness or even death? As Hana decides, so do you!

  • No false bottom! The Multidimensional Underwear Drawer is a full game with five different routes, including one for Yuri-enthusiasts! <3
  • No DLC or microtransactions. You pay once and get EVERYTHING!
  • Every Decision Matters! There is no meaningless decision. Every single one influences your Lovemeter!
  • Atmospheric CGs! Every route will receive their own CG.
  • Linguistic Proficiency! We strive to bring you amusing and intelligent dialogue, both in German and English!
  • How Often Do You Die? With our Death Counter, how many times you have failed to achieve eternal bliss!
  • Rewarding for Achievement Hunters! Over all 5 routes you will be able to unlock a total of 46 achievements!
  • Educational! Over the course of the game, you will encounter several Info-Boxes, filled with funny as well as hilarious explanations for references within the dialogue so that nothing bars your enjoyment of The Multidimensional Underwear Drawer. But don’t worry: You can simply choose to ignore the boxes if you don’t want them ;)

content_descriptors.notes:
This game is a visual novel where explicit themes are primarily conveyed through text and narrative descriptions. It contains depictions of:

- Psychological and Physical Violence: Detailed descriptions of torture within the context of a toxic relationship.
- Self-Harm: Scenarios involving characters committing or contemplating suicide.
- Substance Abuse: Misuse of prescription medication by a central character.
- Sexual Innuendo: Obscene humor and suggestive textual references to sexuality.
- Weapon Violence: Threatening situations involving firearms.

These contents occur optionally within specific branching storylines.

reviews.review:
First half hour, that I've spent, playing this game, was great, and I thought that I've found a true gem among visual novels. Sadly, after that, things got worse. Moments of good humor and interesting story-telling were drowned by frustration and disappointment, that comes not from writing, nor the plot, but game mechanics and the way they are used within the story. This is early access game, obviously, so there may be some changes until final version, but I will judge it for what it is right now.

[h1]Let me start, with few good things:[/h1]

[b]Unique.[/b]  It has interesting concept and it isn't overflowing with cliches, which is great.

[b]Humor.[/b]  Especially during Tymo's route. There are few moments when it feels like creators tried a little too hard (especially with multiple narrators - it wears off really quickly and becomes annoying), but overall, I had a few good laughs, and that's great.

[b]Einar & Tymoteusz.[/b]  Original, surprisingly likable, cute and funny. What's not to like?

[b]One payment.[/b]  I don't like this "trend" that started on app stores and slowly shows up up on Steam, with visual novels cut into pieces and sell separately as episodes or routes. I prefer this "early access" approach much more. That being said...

[h1]Bad things: [/h1]

[b]... price is way too high.[/b]  This is a 23€ game, with five (currently four) routes. From what I've seen (I've played three so far, some few times), you can complete single route in about an hour, sometimes even less, if you get bad ending. That gives us about 5 hour of gameplay, not counting the time that you will spend replaying the game, frustrated, trying to get the right combination of choices to get good ending or at least to not die. Oh, and time you'll spend gaining achievements, since most of them seem literally impossible to get (and I'm not referring to those from missing route). There is only one CG per route, so 5 CGs total. Plus, given the fact, that I know most of in-game music, it's probably royalty-free, although I'm not certain on that one. Either way, it's really hard to see how is it worth 23€.

[b]Guide needed.[/b]  Desperately, I may add. I think this game was intended to be replayed a lot, in order to unlock certain endings, but the problem is, it's getting very frustrating, especially considering that skipping isn't always working as intended and some (most?) outcomes are based on invisible love-meter. For example, on Tymo's route I found myself in a situation, where all of three available choices led to my death. I couldn't do anything about it, so I looked for help. Only thing I gathered from some older discussion, was "Tymo need to love you more". Uh-huh. So you're telling me, I need to replay the whole game, and then out of at least 10 choices or so, pick this right configuration that let me get through, but I don't have any indicator, which choice do what and I can only guess. Okay. If someone is patient enough to do that (or lucky to get it during first try), they will probably move pass this obstacle, but after that, I've decided to give up on playing further until there's some sort of guide or in-game indicator of this mysterious "love-meter". It just seems like massive waste of time.

[b]Dying is not fun.[/b]  Which isn't really surprising, but some games can pull this off well. Here, dying is neither dramatic, nor shocking, nor funny, nor in any way useful, it's a silly way of punishing you for choices that you had no idea could let to this outcome [spoiler] for example, telling Hana's creepy ex-boyfriend to leave, resulted in him killing her. Inviting him in and trying to explain the situation, resulted in r*pe attempt, and then either death or... well... death [/spoiler]. Death counter seems almost like a mockery. This is a visual novel and not "Dark Souls", seriously.

[b]Skipping.[/b]  Isn't working right. Sometimes I wasn't able to skip seen text after reloading a file - I needed to wait for another choice. It's also slow.

[b]No text speed regulation. [/b] Seriously?

[b]Achievements aren't working as intended.[/b] 

[b]Blanche & Furio.[/b] Both of these routes were rushed and bland. There is some nice humor here and there, but not much emotional impact. Furio, with his "I loved you and you have not loved me back, so now that you love me, I don't love you anymore, because reasons" is particularly unlikable and I'm not sure if that was creators intention. Jan's route isn't out yet, but I'm not looking forward to that one.


I still have Einar's route to play, but I will wait with that one till the final version. For now, I cannot recommend this game, not only because of price, but also because of lacking content and frustrating game mechanics.
